# Old National Bank Foundation 20 for 20 Grantee Profiles: Lake Street Council is Minneapolis’ Small Business Incubator


Share:


- Copied!


-
-
-


*As part of its 20th anniversary celebration, and two decades of helping build stronger, more vibrant and prosperous communities, the Old National Bank Foundation in 2026 is donating a total of $20,000 to 20 nonprofit organizations throughout its nine-state footprint, including Lake Street Council in Minneapolis, Minn.*


For nearly six decades, the Lake Street Council has supported the entrepreneurs and small businesses that make Lake Street one of Minneapolis' most vibrant and diverse commercial corridors. Founded in 1967, the organization drives economic development across the six-mile corridor by helping business owners access resources, navigate challenges, and build long-term success.


### 2,000 entrepreneurs and climbing


Home to more than 2,000 entrepreneurs, Lake Street is a vital source of jobs, commerce, and cultural activity in South Minneapolis. The Lake Street Council connects business owners, particularly those from communities of color and historically disinvested communities, with training, technical assistance, funding opportunities, and professional support.


In 2025, the organization:


- Served 220 businesses through direct technical assistance.
- Hosted 25 workshops in Spanish, Somali, and English.
- Connected entrepreneurs with specialized marketing, accounting, and legal services.
- Supported businesses pursuing funding opportunities and building improvements.
- Highlighted more than 150 small businesses through marketing and outreach efforts.
- Promoted Lake Street through its "Lake of 10,000 Lands" campaign and community events.


By supporting entrepreneurs and fostering community connections, the Lake Street Council helps ensure Lake Street remains a thriving destination for opportunity.


### One success story: helping a local business grow


One recent success story is Hoyo Sambusa, a Minneapolis-based business founded to celebrate Somali cuisine while creating employment opportunities for Somali women, refugees, and other immigrants.


Through the “Lake Street Lift” initiative, the Lake Street Council partnered with the Neighborhood Development Center to connect Hoyo Sambusa with consultants who provided operational, branding, and financial guidance as the company launched a new production facility.


"Hoyo's relocation has definitely been helped because of the additional support that is available to companies to spur economic growth and development on the Lake Street corridor," said Mariam Mohamed of Hoyo Sambusa.


Founded in 2015, Hoyo now employs 24 people, distributes products to more than 60 stores, and serves more than 30 Minnesota school districts. The company is working toward doubling production to 8,000 sambusas – the deep-fried savory pastries, typically filled with spiced meats – per day.


### Lake Street Council and Old National: Supporting Entrepreneurs Through Partnership


“Old National Bank has been an important partner for the Lake Street Council, as well as a vital resource for Lake Street businesses,” said ZoeAna Martinez, Senior Community Engagement Manager for the Lake Street Council. “Their support has helped strengthen our technical assistance and business outreach efforts, ensuring we can meet the needs of the diverse entrepreneurs that make up the Lake Street corridor.”


The partnership between the Old National Bank Foundation and Lake Street Council reflects a shared commitment to building stronger communities and expanding opportunities for local businesses. Old National has also helped bring the community together through sponsorship of events that celebrate the businesses, cultures, and neighborhoods that make Lake Street unique.


“Our ‘20 for 20’ campaign recognizes 20 organizations that have helped strengthen communities and expand opportunity through their partnership with the Old National Bank Foundation,” said Old National Bank Foundation President Joe Kiser. “Their leadership, innovation, and commitment to serving others reflect the very best of what can happen when communities come together around a shared purpose. As we celebrate the Foundation’s 20th anniversary, these organizations represent the many communities, causes, and partnerships that have shaped the Foundation’s work over the past two decades.”


To learn more about the Lake Street Council,[click here](https://www.lakestreetcouncil.org/) .


Each year, the Old National Bank Foundation endeavors to fund as many initiatives that meet our funding priorities as possible across our footprint.
